description: Synthetic outputs captured before the input-quality layer

result.default_classification_context: Technical reference at 0.5 only; not a diagnosis.
result.reference_interpretation: Below both sensitivity-oriented development-derived screening references.
limitations: This is model-based decision support, not a diagnosis of diabetes.
Thresholds are development-derived operating references, not clinically validated clinical cutoffs.
SHAP explains model behavior, not causation; contributions are log-odds, not probability changes.
Incomplete inputs may reduce robustness: completed temporal validation showed lower performance among participants with missing Core-10 predictors.
The target is physician-diagnosed diabetes (DIQ010), not prospective diabetes incidence; intended population is adults.

model_derived_risk.label: LOW model-derived risk
model_derived_risk.basis: Project-defined interpretation of frozen sensitivity-oriented development operating references; not incident diabetes risk.
model_derived_risk.disclaimer: Low, Moderate, and High are model-derived decision-support strata based on development operating references. They are not diagnostic categories or clinically validated risk thresholds.

clinical_follow_up.text: Continue routine preventive care. Discuss diabetes screening according to your age, history, previous results and clinician advice; a LOW model-derived result does not rule out diabetes.
clinical_follow_up.rationale: Avoid false reassurance or suppression of clinically indicated screening
source_labels: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, section 2: Diagnosis and Classification
Project-defined model-derived CDSS workflow v1

clinical_follow_up.text: Seek clinical assessment if symptoms such as increased thirst, frequent urination or unexplained weight loss develop, or if other health concerns arise, regardless of the model result.
clinical_follow_up.rationale: Symptoms and concerns override reassurance from a classification score
source_labels: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, section 2: Diagnosis and Classification

monitoring.text: Review weight, blood pressure and metabolic health during usual preventive visits; follow the monitoring schedule agreed with your clinician.

feature_aware.trigger_description: Observed adult age >=20 and observed BMI >=25 kg/m²
feature_aware.text: The entered BMI meets a conventional adult weight-review threshold. Consider discussing individualized weight-management support; BMI alone does not establish a disease or the right plan for you.
feature_aware.rationale: Observed BMI supports a contextual weight discussion, not a treatment assignment
source_labels: NIH/NIDDK: Health Tips for Adults
ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, section 5: Positive Health Behaviors

feature_aware.text: You reported current smoking. Consider evidence-based smoking-cessation counseling or support through a qualified health professional. This prototype does not select medicines.
feature_aware.rationale: Cessation support follows the reported smoking status, not its SHAP contribution
source_labels: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, section 5: Positive Health Behaviors

feature_aware.trigger_description: Observed adult age >=20 and systolic >=120 OR diastolic >=80 mmHg
feature_aware.text: An entered blood-pressure measurement may warrant review. Confirm measurement technique and discuss repeat assessment with a healthcare professional; these inputs do not diagnose hypertension.
feature_aware.rationale: Use conventional elevated-BP review conventions without labeling a disease
source_labels: 2025 AHA/ACC multisociety blood-pressure guideline

feature_aware.trigger_description: Observed adult age >=20; waist >101.6 cm for sex=1 or >88.9 cm for sex=2
feature_aware.text: The entered waist measurement exceeds a conventional adult review threshold. Consider discussing central adiposity in your individual clinical context; these thresholds do not apply equally to every person or population.
feature_aware.rationale: NIDDK >40/>35 inch conventions converted exactly using 2.54 cm/inch; no race-specific treatment
source_labels: NIH/NIDDK: Health Tips for Adults

feature_aware.trigger_description: Observed adult age >=20; total cholesterol >=200 mg/dL OR HDL <40 for sex=1 / <50 for sex=2
feature_aware.text: An entered lipid measurement may warrant review of the full lipid profile with a clinician. These values alone do not diagnose a lipid disorder or establish a need for treatment.
feature_aware.rationale: Conventional adult reference values prompt a contextual review only
source_labels: NIH/MedlinePlus: Cholesterol Levels—What You Need to Know
